situation:
You are the marketing director for HALLOWAY FORM WORKS, a 3D printing prototype shop in its third generation of family ownership. The shop prints test parts for restaurant equipment makers and food-service chains, and two cousins own it together under the partnership agreement their grandparents wrote.

One of those cousins is the managing partner (judge), who has asked you to recommend where the shop's marketing goes next. The partnership agreement requires both partners to agree in writing before the shop takes on debt, and the other partner has said plainly that borrowing against a forecast is not how three generations kept the shop open.

NORTHVALE KITCHENS, a regional restaurant chain, wants HALLOWAY to print the serving vessels and menu-item packaging for a new store format and to move from prototypes into production runs. Taking the work means buying two production printers on a five-year loan and rebranding the shop as a production supplier, with a new slogan and a campaign aimed at food-service buyers.

The chain has committed only to its four test markets. The nationwide rollout its forecast assumes has not been signed, and if the new format stops after those test markets the shop owes five years of loan payments with the two production printers idle. The other partner's written consent would have to be won first.

Staying a prototype shop instead means spending the same money on a marketing plan that reaches new clients through trade shows, an email program, and the shop's own website. That gives up the NORTHVALE KITCHENS order to a competitor, and the returns come slowly, a few small clients at a time. The managing partner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the managing partner (judge) of HALLOWAY FORM WORKS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You are the third generation of your family to run the shop, and you own it with your cousin under the partnership agreement your grandparents wrote. You want to hear which marketing plan the marketing director recommends — moving into production runs for NORTHVALE KITCHENS under a new brand and slogan, or staying a prototype shop and marketing to a wider set of clients — and you want to hear how that recommendation would actually be carried out, step by step.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What is the first step in putting your recommendation in place?
Who at the shop does the work, and in what order?
